name: Multi Page Auto Advance for Gravity Forms
author: Frog Eat Fly

sections.description:
Multi Page Auto Advance helps you create faster, easier Gravity Forms multi-page forms by moving visitors to the next page after they answer a trigger field.

Instead of making users answer a question, find the Next button, click again, and wait for the next step, this Gravity Forms add-on can automatically advance the form after a radio button or dropdown selection.

Use it for lead forms, intake forms, quizzes, surveys, quote forms, onboarding forms, and any Gravity Forms workflow where fewer clicks can improve completion.

What the free plugin does

  • Auto-advance Gravity Forms pages after radio button choices
  • Auto-advance Gravity Forms pages after dropdown selections
  • Create a smoother one-question-at-a-time form experience
  • Reduce extra Next button clicks in multi-page forms
  • Configure auto-advance from the Gravity Forms field settings panel
  • Keep your forms built in Gravity Forms instead of moving to a separate form builder

Common use cases

  • Gravity Forms auto next after a radio button answer
  • Gravity Forms auto advance after a dropdown choice
  • Multi-step lead generation forms
  • Client intake forms with fewer clicks
  • Quiz and survey flows
  • Quote request forms
  • Typeform-style WordPress forms built with Gravity Forms

Pro ($39.99/year)

Upgrade to Pro when your Gravity Forms workflow needs more field types and richer multi-page behavior.

Everything from Free, plus:

  1. Product field support
  2. Poll and quiz support
  3. Checkbox field auto-advance
  4. Text and number field support
  5. Conditional logic support
  6. Gravity Forms Conversational Forms Add-On support
  7. Transition animations
  8. Step color controls

[GET PRO]

Plus ($59/year or $225 lifetime)

Everything from Pro, plus upgraded conversational form functionality for more advanced one-question-at-a-time experiences.

sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/multipage-auto-advance directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Open or create a Gravity Forms multi-page form.
  4. Add a Radio Button or Dropdown field.
  5. Open the field settings and enable Auto Advance.
  6. Save the form and test the frontend flow.

Once enabled, the selected field can trigger Gravity Forms to move to the next page automatically.
sections.faq:
Which Gravity Forms fields are supported in the free version?

The free version supports radio button fields and dropdown fields.

Pro adds support for additional field types, including checkboxes, text fields, number fields, products, polls, quizzes, conditional logic, animations, and Gravity Forms Conversational Forms Add-On workflows.

Does this work with Gravity Forms multi-page forms?

Yes. Multi Page Auto Advance is built for Gravity Forms multi-page forms. It helps move visitors from one page or step to the next after they answer a supported trigger field.

Can I hide the Next button in Gravity Forms?

Yes. The plugin includes settings for hiding manual navigation buttons where appropriate, so visitors can move through the form by answering questions instead of clicking Next after every step.

How do I set up Gravity Forms auto-advance?

  1. Create a new form or open an existing one
  2. Click any Radio Button or Dropdown question that you want to be a trigger.
  3. Check the box for Auto Advance in the settings for the question.
  4. Save the form and test it on the frontend.

Can I build a Typeform-style form with Gravity Forms?

Yes. Multi Page Auto Advance can help create a more conversational, one-question-at-a-time Gravity Forms experience. The free version supports basic radio and dropdown auto-advance, while Pro and Plus add more advanced field and conversational form support.

Does auto-advance replace Gravity Forms?

No. This is an add-on for Gravity Forms. You still build and manage your forms in Gravity Forms, and this plugin adds auto-advance behavior to supported fields.

Is it possible to have two triggers on one form page?

Yes, as long as both are not set as “required”. If both are ‘required’ then the form will not advance to the next page and an error message will show.
